components.name: Customer Portal Frontend
components.purpose: Host the static web assets for the customer-facing portal, ensuring mobile responsiveness and fast delivery.
components.rationale: AWS Amplify Hosting provides a fully managed service for deploying and hosting single-page applications and static websites, with built-in CDN capabilities for performance.
trade_offs: Limited server-side logic capabilities directly within Amplify Hosting.
components.security_considerations: Leverage AWS WAF for protection against common web exploits.

components.name: Backend API Services
components.purpose: Provide serverless API endpoints for portal functionalities like tracking, invoices, payments, and queries.
components.rationale: AWS Lambda offers a scalable, cost-effective serverless compute service that automatically scales with demand, suitable for event-driven API requests.
trade_offs: Potential cold start latencies for infrequently accessed functions.
components.security_considerations: Implement least privilege IAM roles for each Lambda function and integrate with AWS Secrets Manager for sensitive data.

components.name: Customer Data Database
components.purpose: Store customer profiles, portal-specific settings, and potentially cached data for tracking and invoices.
components.rationale: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition provides high performance, availability, and scalability for relational data, suitable for critical customer information.
trade_offs: Higher cost compared to standard RDS for smaller workloads.
components.security_considerations: Encrypt data at rest and in transit, and restrict access using VPC security groups and IAM policies.

components.name: User Authentication and Authorization
components.purpose: Manage user registration, login, and access control for portal customers.
components.rationale: Amazon Cognito provides a scalable and secure user directory service with support for standard authentication flows and MFA.
trade_offs: Customization options can be complex for advanced scenarios.
components.security_considerations: Enforce strong password policies, MFA, and integrate with AWS WAF for protection against credential stuffing.

components.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
components.name: API Gateway
components.purpose: Provide a unified, secure entry point for all API requests to the backend services.
components.rationale: Amazon API Gateway handles API routing, request/response transformation, authorization, and throttling, offloading these concerns from backend services.
trade_offs: Can add complexity for very simple API deployments.
components.security_considerations: Implement API key usage, JWT authorizers, and integrate with AWS WAF for API protection.

components.name: TMS Integration Proxy
components.purpose: Securely expose and manage access to the existing TMS APIs for shipment tracking.
components.rationale: Amazon API Gateway acts as a secure proxy, allowing controlled access to internal systems and handling authentication/authorization for external calls.
trade_offs: Adds an additional layer of latency compared to direct integration.
components.security_considerations: Implement strict access controls, API keys, and potentially AWS PrivateLink for secure connectivity to the TMS.

components.name: Content Delivery Network
components.purpose: Distribute static portal assets globally to reduce latency and improve load times for users.
components.rationale: Amazon CloudFront provides a global content delivery network that caches content at edge locations, improving performance and reducing origin load.
trade_offs: Configuration complexity for advanced caching behaviors.
components.security_considerations: Integrate with AWS WAF and AWS Shield for DDoS protection and web application security.

components.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
components.name: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC)
components.purpose: Provide a logically isolated network for all cloud resources, enabling fine-grained control over network traffic.
components.rationale: Amazon VPC allows for the creation of a private, secure network environment within AWS, essential for isolating application components.
trade_offs: Requires careful planning of subnets, routing tables, and network ACLs.
components.security_considerations: Implement network segmentation, security groups, and network ACLs to control inbound and outbound traffic.

components.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
components.name: Monitoring and Logging
components.purpose: Collect logs, metrics, and traces from all application components for operational visibility and troubleshooting.
components.rationale: Amazon CloudWatch provides comprehensive monitoring capabilities, allowing for centralized collection and analysis of operational data.
trade_offs: Can incur significant costs for high-volume log ingestion and retention.
components.security_considerations: Ensure logs are encrypted at rest and access to monitoring data is restricted via IAM policies.

components.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
components.name: Secrets Management
components.purpose: Securely store and manage sensitive credentials and API keys for application components.
components.rationale: AWS Secrets Manager provides a centralized service for managing secrets, with automatic rotation and fine-grained access control.
trade_offs: Adds a dependency and slight overhead for secret retrieval.
components.security_considerations: Integrate with IAM to ensure only authorized services and roles can retrieve specific secrets.

components.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
components.name: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
components.purpose: Protect the customer portal and APIs from common web exploits and bots.
components.rationale: AWS WAF helps protect web applications or APIs from common web exploits that may affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources.
trade_offs: Requires careful rule configuration to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.
components.security_considerations: Regularly review and update WAF rules to address new threats and vulnerabilities.

components.name: Finance System Integration Proxy
components.purpose: Securely expose and manage access to the existing Finance System APIs for invoice retrieval.
components.rationale: Amazon API Gateway provides a secure and managed interface for integrating with internal systems, abstracting the backend complexity.
trade_offs: Adds an additional layer of latency compared to direct integration.
components.security_considerations: Implement strict access controls, API keys, and potentially AWS PrivateLink for secure connectivity to the Finance System.

components.name: Payment Gateway Integration
components.purpose: Facilitate secure communication with the external payment gateway for online invoice payments.
components.rationale: Amazon API Gateway can act as a secure intermediary for external payment integrations, handling request routing and security.
trade_offs: Requires careful handling of sensitive payment data and PCI compliance considerations.
components.security_considerations: Ensure all communication is encrypted (HTTPS) and sensitive payment data is not stored within the portal's direct control.

environments.dev: Development environments will be isolated, allowing developers to build and test features independently.
environments.test: Test environments will mirror production as closely as possible for integration and user acceptance testing.
environments.prod: Production environment will be highly available and secure, hosting the live customer portal. All environments will be provisioned using Infrastructure as Code.

deployment_runtime.validation_reason: The target cloud platform is assumed (ASM_04).
deployment_runtime.text: The solution will leverage AWS serverless services for deployment and runtime. The frontend (ARC_01) will be hosted on AWS Amplify Hosting, providing continuous deployment capabilities. Backend API services (ARC_02) will be deployed as AWS Lambda functions, managed via AWS API Gateway (ARC_05). Infrastructure will be defined using Infrastructure as Code (e.g., AWS CloudFormation or AWS CDK) to ensure consistency across dev, test, and prod environments. Containerization (e.g., AWS Fargate) could be an alternative for backend services if more control over runtime environment is required.

availability_scalability.validation_reason: User and shipment volumes are assumed (ASM_01).
availability_scalability.text: The architecture is designed for high availability and scalability to support assumed mid-market volumes (ASM_01). AWS Amplify Hosting (ARC_01) and Amazon CloudFront (ARC_07) inherently provide global distribution and scalability. AWS Lambda (ARC_02) automatically scales to handle varying request loads. Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition (ARC_03) offers high availability with multi-AZ deployments and read replicas. Amazon API Gateway (ARC_05) and Amazon Cognito (ARC_04) are managed services that scale automatically. Elastic Load Balancing and Auto Scaling will be implicitly used by these managed services.

backup_dr.validation_reason: Backup and DR requirements were not explicitly stated by the customer.
backup_dr.text: Backup and disaster recovery strategies will be implemented for critical data. Amazon Aurora (ARC_03) provides automated backups, point-in-time recovery, and can be configured for cross-region replication for disaster recovery. AWS S3 (implicitly used by Amplify Hosting and CloudFront) provides high durability for static assets. Lambda functions (ARC_02) are stateless, simplifying DR. A recovery time objective (RTO) and recovery point objective (RPO) will need to be defined by the customer.

observability.validation_reason: Observability requirements are inferred from standard practices.
observability.text: Comprehensive observability will be achieved using Amazon CloudWatch (ARC_09) for collecting logs, metrics, and traces from all components. CloudWatch Logs will centralize application and infrastructure logs. CloudWatch Metrics will monitor performance and resource utilization. AWS X-Ray will be integrated with AWS Lambda (ARC_02) and Amazon API Gateway (ARC_05) to provide end-to-end tracing for requests, aiding in performance analysis and troubleshooting. Alarms will be configured in CloudWatch to notify operations teams of critical issues.

security_controls.validation_reason: Security and authentication standards are assumed (ASM_05).
security_controls.text: Security is a foundational aspect, with controls implemented across multiple layers. AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) will enforce least privilege access for all AWS resources. Amazon Cognito (ARC_04) will handle user authentication with MFA. AWS WAF (ARC_11) will protect the portal and APIs from common web exploits. All data will be encrypted at rest (e.g., Amazon Aurora, S3) and in transit (HTTPS/TLS). AWS Secrets Manager (ARC_10) will securely store and manage application secrets. Network segmentation will be enforced using Amazon VPC (ARC_08) with security groups and network ACLs. Regular security audits and vulnerability scanning will be performed.
